gaps.sentence: My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

gaps.sentence: ___ poverty remains a serious problem in many large cities.
gaps.explanation: Uncountable abstract nouns in a general sense take no article.

gaps.sentence: He behaves as if he were ___ owner of the company.
gaps.explanation: 'The owner' — there is one owner, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: She earns her living as ___ journalist.
gaps.explanation: Jobs after 'as' take a/an: as a journalist.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.

gaps.sentence: He drives ___ old van that is always breaking down.
gaps.explanation: 'An old van' — 'old' begins with a vowel sound. The second gap is 'the axle'.

gaps.sentence: The car crashed into a wall at ___ speed of 90 km/h.
gaps.explanation: 'At a speed of…' — 'a' is part of this fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: She goes to the gym twice ___ week.
gaps.explanation: 'Twice a week' — rates take 'a' (= per). The other gap is 'the gym'.
